name: Centrism
summary: Centrism is a position between left and right that favours moderate, gradual and pragmatic reform. Its best-documented strands are Third Way and radical centrism, which accept market economies while keeping a liberal welfare state, and stress opportunity with responsibility. It has no fixed program, so many policy answers are inferences.
scope: Mainstream Western centrism as documented in Third Way politics (Giddens, Blair, Clinton, Schroeder) and radical centrism (Satin, Halstead and Lind, Avlon). Excludes parties merely labelled centrist, centrist populism and agrarian or Christian-democratic variants. As a positional label rather than a program, many answers are low-confidence inferences.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Centrists support a liberal welfare state; universal coverage is inferred as a common but not defining centrist position.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Moderates accept some wage floors but split on a substantial rise; inferred from balanced economic stance.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Radical centrists favour market-based solutions with strong oversight in the public interest, so neither side is taken outright.

public-ownership.rationale: Third Way centrism accepts competitive markets and public-private partnerships rather than broad nationalisation.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Third Way figures cut some taxes to attract investment, while other centrists accept moderate redistribution; adherents are split.

unions-good.rationale: Clinton praised firms sharing gains with workers but centrists have no fixed union line; inferred.

property-fundamental.rationale: Centrism sits close to liberalism, which values property; inferred, not stressed.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Strong oversight is favoured alongside market solutions, so tighter regulation is a case-by-case question.

cut-welfare.rationale: Third Way reform favours workfare and a hand-up rather than cutting welfare outright.

worker-ownership.rationale: Not a centrist goal; inferred from acceptance of conventional market enterprise.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; moderates are split between security and liberty.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed as a core issue; centrist opinion is divided.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; centrists are divided between liberal speech norms and social-harm concerns.

strong-leader.rationale: Radical centrists want grounded movements and institutional reform rather than a single charismatic leader.

state-harmful.rationale: Centrists support a liberal welfare state and institutional reform, and reject abolishing the state.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from mainstream centre-left Third Way politicians such as Clinton; contested among centrists.

empower-police-military.rationale: Not addressed; centrists are split on this.

decide-locally.rationale: No fixed centrist position on decentralisation; inferred.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from moderate, evidence-oriented reform attitudes.

traditional-family.rationale: Clinton stressed family and parental responsibility, yet social liberal centrists are less traditional; split.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Social liberalism is a main centrist variant, so legalisation is inferred as the mainstream view.

abortion-legal.rationale: Social liberal centrism leans pro-choice in most cases; inferred.

more-religion-public.rationale: Inferred from liberal-leaning centrism favouring secular public institutions, though Christian democrats differ.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Social liberal centrism generally supports measures against discrimination; inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Not addressed; moderates are split between cosmopolitan and traditional views.

gradual-change.rationale: Centrists favour gradual change and prioritise prudence in institutional reform.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; centrist parties are split.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: European centrist parties supported integration and the EU; inferred more broadly.

free-trade.rationale: The Third Way accepts global economic integration and works to attract investment within it.

nation-first.rationale: Radical centrists support global engagement; inferred.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Third Way leaders such as Clinton and Blair supported intervention; inferred for the mainstream.

open-borders.rationale: Moderate centrists do not advocate abolishing borders; inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: Third Way centrism prizes growth and the revenue it generates.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Environmental protection is a Third Way theme but drastic action is not defining; split.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Radical centrism is pragmatic and not techno-utopian; inferred.

revolution-justified.rationale: Centrists favour gradual, prudent reform over revolutionary change.

experts-over-public.rationale: Evidence-based policy appeals to centrists, but they also want democratic legitimacy; split.

central-planning.rationale: Third Way accepts competitive markets as the main engine of wealth.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred from acceptance of conventional markets with public-private partnerships.

land-value-tax.rationale: A single-tax system is not a centrist position; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Third Way stresses work and responsibility rather than unconditional payments, though some radical centrists back it.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Third Way accepts globalisation and free trade; inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Markets are the main engine of wealth, with state action where markets fail.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Centrism has no documented position on this; adherents are divided, so it is answered neutrally.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Centrism rejects abolishing the market economy.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Centrism accepts conventional institutions and fiscal discipline; inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Third Way relies on markets, not state-run wage and price bargaining; inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: Centrism operates within plural party democracy.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not addressed; centrists in monarchies accept it, others do not.

democracy-best.rationale: Clinton's New Covenant stresses democratic community and citizen involvement; centrism is rooted in plural democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Centrists favour institutional reform within representative systems; inferred.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not a centrist position; inferred from its moderate, pragmatic and liberal-democratic outlook.

political-violence-never.rationale: Inferred from the moderate, prudential, gradualist outlook.

separate-church-state.rationale: Inferred from liberal-leaning centrism, though Christian democrats differ.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Not centrist; inferred from liberal pluralism.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Centrism supports a liberal welfare state and public institutions.

military-superiority.rationale: Centrism has no documented position on this; adherents are divided, so it is answered neutrally.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Clinton frames the country as one community going up or down together, rejecting class conflict.

national-rebirth.rationale: Radical centrists reject mass emotional radicalism in favour of realism; inferred.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Not a centrist position; inferred from its moderate, pragmatic and liberal-democratic outlook.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Centrism has no documented position on this; adherents are divided, so it is answered neutrally.

revive-national-language.rationale: Centrism has no documented position on this; adherents are divided, so it is answered neutrally.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not a Third Way aim; inferred.

school-vouchers.rationale: Radical centrists back school choice but other centrists oppose; split.

economic-freedom.rationale: Third Way accepts markets and economic liberalism; inferred.

force-without-un.rationale: Centrism has no documented position on this; adherents are divided, so it is answered neutrally.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Pragmatism favoured, but no fixed epistemological claim.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Centrism has no documented position on this; adherents are divided, so it is answered neutrally.

dominated-front.rationale: Not a centrist position; inferred from its moderate, pragmatic and liberal-democratic outlook.

workers-nation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from centrist moderation.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred: Third Way and radical centrism accept liberal equality under law, though gender roles are not a documented centrist theme.

ban-interest.rationale: Inferred: centrists accept market economies and their financial markets, with regulation rather than prohibition.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Centrism sits within the liberal democratic mainstream, which treats people alike before the law.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Inferred: Third Way and radical centrism see the state as a means to common goals and pragmatic reform, not a class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred: Third Way and radical centrists favor pragmatic, balanced energy policy rather than either expansion or phase-out.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inferred: centrists favor integration with opportunity and responsibility, not forced abandonment of culture.

elite-replacement.rationale: Inferred: centrists stress evidence and pragmatism, and reject conspiratorial claims.

proportional-representation.rationale: Inferred: radical centrists and centrist parties often back electoral reform, though many accept existing systems.

national-mission.rationale: Inferred: Third Way politics stresses cooperation and globalisation over national missions, though some centrist leaders speak of national leadership.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred: Third Way centre-left strands endorse equal opportunity and anti-discrimination, but centrists avoid structural framings.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Inferred: centrists defend democratic institutions and compromise, though radical centrism criticizes partisan political classes.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred from the liberal commitment to individual rights shared across centrist strands.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from centrist support for rule of law and liberal institutions.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Centrists keep a liberal welfare state and regulated markets, so confining government to defense, justice and property is rejected.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Mainstream centrists back liberal, inclusive values and reject racial discrimination; inferred from the Third Way's social-inclusion stance.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Third Way and radical centrism accept equal rights and opportunity for all as a baseline; inferred.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Centrism has no view on this Marxist debate.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Centrists are split on how to classify settler states and offer no common position.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Liberal-leaning centrists favor equal treatment under common law; inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Moderate liberal values suggest freedom to change religion; inferred.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: No centrist position; pragmatic liberal values lean against bans on legal practices; inferred.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Pragmatic centrists tend toward secular public schools, though practice varies by country; inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Centrists favor limited, pragmatic government and are not committed to growing the state; inferred.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Moderate liberal democracy rests on consent, but centrism has no stated doctrine of legitimacy; inferred.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Centrists generally trust expertise and evidence-based policy over power-based accounts of truth; inferred from pragmatic, non-ideological centrism.

trade-surplus.rationale: Third Way centrists embrace open markets and globalisation, so a surplus is not a policy goal; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Centrist liberal-democratic thought supports minority rights and rejects expulsion of minorities; inferred from its liberal welfare-state commitments.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Centrists accept state coercion for law enforcement, taxation and security, so an absolute ban on initiating force is not their position; inferred.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Third Way stresses opportunity with community and responsibility rather than competition as the engine of progress; inferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Moderate defenders of constitutional order commonly accept limits on parties that aim to overthrow it; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Centrist liberal-democratic politics broadly values protection from arbitrary power; not a defining centrist theme, so inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: Centrism favours moderate, balanced institutions and gradual reform over concentrated power.

vanguard-party.rationale: Centrists favour gradual, democratic and pluralist reform and reject revolutionary vanguard politics.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Third Way centrists favour opportunity for all and welfare-to-work rather than first priority to the poor; adherents are split.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Third Way governments kept the Thatcher-era right to buy and favoured asset ownership; inferred from the Third Way emphasis on opportunity and responsibility.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Third Way governments such as New Labour kept ballot requirements and limits on industrial action; inferred from their acceptance of market flexibility.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Centrists locate poverty in unequal opportunity and policy rather than numbers of people; inferred from the opportunity-with-responsibility approach.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Third Way and radical centrism accept multicultural, open societies; inferred, not a defining centrist claim.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Centrism works within representative liberal democracy and offers no support for sortition; inferred from its moderate institutionalism.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Centrists defend liberal democratic legal protections and gradual reform over emergency measures; inferred from their liberal-democratic commitments.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Centrists accept market economies and prefer market-based solutions with oversight, so broad price ceilings are disfavoured; inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: Centrism is a liberal-democratic position that keeps a free press independent of government.

party-commands-army.rationale: Centrism rests on constitutional liberal democracy, in which the armed forces serve the state and not a party.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Centrists are split between liberal-integrationist and more restrictive centre-right strands; no settled centrist position.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Inferred from pragmatic moderation favouring competitive pay for public service.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Inferred from centrists' rejection of partisan rigidity and preference for independent, cross-party judgment.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Centrism is documented as supporting European integration and global cooperation.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Inferred from support for liberal democracy with legislative checks on executive power.

clerical-rule.rationale: Inferred from centrism's liberal-democratic, secular political order.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Inferred from Third Way support for national security and rejection of defeatism; not a doctrine.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred from liberal-democratic moderation, which resists state policing of art; not a defining issue.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred from moderate preference for institutional checks on executive power; contested.

recall-officials.rationale: Inferred as split: radical centrists favour political reform, but centrists have no common view on recall.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Third Way governments such as Clinton and Blair kept NATO alliances; inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Centrists accept markets and property; a ban on renting is inferred to be rejected.

people-in-arms.rationale: Inferred: pragmatic centrists favour professional defence forces.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Inferred: centrism has no view on moral geography and favours pragmatism over romanticism.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Inferred from the pragmatic respect for expertise and rejection of populist anti-elitism.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Not addressed by the ideology; adherents are split.

death-penalty.rationale: Adherents are split: Clinton supported the death penalty while many European centrists oppose it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from a liberal welfare-state and moderate-reform outlook.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Inferred: pragmatic centrists generally want science taught in science class.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed; centrists are split between liberty and harm-reduction arguments.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred from moderate liberal views on inclusion.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed; centrists split between pluralism and common rules.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not addressed by the ideology; adherents are split.

notes: Strands differ: Christian-democratic and centre-right variants lean more conservative, centre-left Third Way variants more social-democratic. Centrism is a positional label, so most answers are inferences.
